title: U.S. House · Utah's 3rd District
area: Southern and eastern Utah under the congressional map first used in 2026, drawn by a Third District Court after the Legislature's 2021 map was struck down; largely overlaps the old 2nd District, including Cedar City, St. George and southeastern Utah.

context.text: Utah's congressional map was redrawn for 2026 by court order in League of Women Voters v. Utah State Legislature. Incumbent Celeste Maloy — who previously represented the old 2nd District — is running for this newly drawn 3rd District. Maloy defeated Phil Lyman 65.7%-34.3% in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary.

candidates.name: Celeste Maloy
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Phil Lyman 65.7%-34.3% in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary

priorities.text: Says legislation she helped pass delivered "the largest tax cut in American history," increasing take-home pay by about $10,000 per year for the average family and cutting taxes for 88% of seniors on Social Security.
Says she has voted to cut federal spending and eliminate wasteful spending, citing $9 billion a year in savings from her work on the Appropriations Committee.
Says she supports giving Utah more control over federal lands and resources, and has voted to expand domestic energy production including oil, gas and refining capacity.

positions.summary: Opposes stricter gun laws, saying she will defend Second Amendment rights against what she calls "gun grabbers" in Washington.
positions.quote: She will fight the gun grabbers in Washington DC and defend our constitutional rights.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations (Vice Chair, Interior Environment and Related Agencies subcommittee) and the House Committee on Natural Resources in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: Federal key floor votes and FEC finance totals for this sitting member of Congress are added separately by script.

candidates.name: Kent Udell
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot after the primary was canceled

priorities.text: Water: calls protecting the Great Salt Lake and Colorado River water supply one of his top priorities.
priorities.quote: This is one of my top priorities.

priorities.text: Public lands: says he would defend public lands and long-term stewardship.
priorities.quote: I will defend public lands and long-term stewardship in cooperation with the needs of my constituents.

priorities.text: Anti-corruption: does not take corporate PAC money and calls for transparency, accountability and ethics reforms.
priorities.quote: I will fight for transparency, accountability, and ethics reforms that put American interests, not special interests, first.

positions.summary: Supports the Second Amendment and also supports gun safety training, safe storage and red flag laws.
positions.quote: I support gun safety training, safe storage, and Red Flag Laws, not fear-based political posturing.

positions.summary: Calls for reforming health care by learning from other countries and expanding programs such as Medicare so they are accessible to all.
positions.quote: We should learn from those examples to reform our health care system, diminishing the influence of insurance companies, and expand programs, such as Medicare, to be accessible to all.

candidates.researchNotes: Statements and priorities from Udell's campaign website (kentudell.com) and the Salt Lake Tribune candidate questionnaire (Oct. 12, 2026). In the questionnaire he also wrote 'I support either universal healthcare or Medicare for all.' (healthcare position above is from the earlier campaign-site quote).

statements.quote: I propose the Carbon Fee & American Return (CFAR): charge polluters for the CO2 they release and return that revenue directly to Americans.
statements.context: In the Salt Lake Tribune candidate questionnaire, Oct. 12, 2026

statements.quote: Our immigration system is broken, but cruelty, chaos, and political theater are not solutions.
Push for federal funding for childcare including tax credits and deduction of childcare costs below a threshold income.
statements.context: In the Salt Lake Tribune candidate questionnaire, Oct. 12, 2026

statements.quote: I support initiatives that focus on building starter homes in communities with access to family-friendly resources

candidates.name: Cassie Easley
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the April 25, 2026 Constitution Party convention

priorities.text: Says her core campaign messages are "We the People," the Second Amendment, and the Sixteenth Amendment.

Says a representative's only two responsibilities are fidelity to the Constitution and to the will of the people they represent, and that federal spending on anything outside constitutionally enumerated powers should not be funded.
priorities.quote: Anything that falls outside of the Constitutional boundaries should not be funded.

candidates.researchNotes: Salt Lake Tribune candidate questionnaire (Oct. 12, 2026) reviewed in addition to Ballotpedia; her answers focus on federal spending, water, surveillance and data centers and do not squarely take a side on the guide's other issue statements. No campaign website found. No campaign website was found; biography draws on her 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.

statements.quote: I am a strong proponent of the 2nd Amendment, without it there is no way to protect the rest.
statements.context: In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

candidates.name: Michael Stoddard
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the April 18, 2026 Libertarian Party convention; previously a Libertarian candidate for this district in 2022

priorities.text: Government audit: proposes an annual independent external audit of the federal government.
priorities.quote: Require an annual independent external audit by international accounting firms

priorities.text: Sound money: proposes ending the legal-tender requirement and opening the Federal Reserve to an independent audit.
priorities.quote: Open the Federal Reserve's books to independent external audit

priorities.text: Taxes: proposes indexing savings and investment to inflation.
priorities.quote: I'll work to index savings and investment to the dollar's decline

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website (2amike4congress.org) reviewed. He did not answer the Salt Lake Tribune candidate questionnaire. His planks (accountability, sound money, Second Amendment, taxes, health care) do not squarely take a side on the guide's issue statements, so no stances are recorded. No biographical detail (birthplace, education or career), campaign website content, or Candidate Connection survey was found beyond his ballot listing and prior 2022 candidacy.

statements.quote: Protect the armed body of the people from both federal overreach and state-level disarmament
statements.context: On his campaign website (Second Amendment plank)

statements.quote: I'll unchain coverage from employment, re-legalize real catastrophic insurance for the rare disaster, restore honest up-front prices, and fund the genuinely uninsurable in the daylight instead of hiding them inside everyone's premium.
statements.context: On his campaign website (Health Care plank)

candidates.name: Adonis Hooslyn

priorities.text: Affordability: lower the costs of housing, groceries and utilities.
priorities.quote: Lower the costs of housing, groceries, and utilities.

priorities.text: Healthcare: transition to Medicare for All.
priorities.quote: Healthcare must be a right, not a privilege tied to employment or wealth.

priorities.text: Jobs and AI: protect and create jobs while regulating AI development.
priorities.quote: Protect and create jobs while regulating AI development.

priorities.text: Corruption: demand transparent investigations and oppose using taxpayer funds for foreign wars.
priorities.quote: Demand justice, transparent investigations, and oppose using taxpayer funds for foreign wars.

positions.summary: Calls for transitioning to a Medicare for All system.
positions.quote: Transition to a Medicare 4 All System.

positions.summary: Lists increasing taxes on billionaires among his additional priorities.
positions.quote: Increase taxes for billionaires to ensure they pay their fair share toward our national prosperity.

positions.summary: Lists abolishing ICE and reallocating its funds among his additional priorities.
positions.quote: Abolish ICE and reallocate funds toward Core 4 policies that protect American families.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and priorities from Hooslyn's campaign website (hooslynforhouse.com), which lists four core policies plus additional priorities. He answered the Salt Lake Tribune candidate questionnaire (Oct. 12, 2026), which did not add further matches to the guide's issue list.
